key_insight: Sequence-to-sequence, attention-based deep models (transformer-like) are the most effective at mapping noisy measured quantum-circuit output distributions to mitigated distributions that are closer to the ideal.
problem_solved: Reduces noise-induced errors in probability distributions obtained from measured quantum circuits, improving the fidelity of classical estimates derived from near-term noisy quantum hardware.
method: Compare a range of architectures (from fully connected networks to transformers) and multiple design/training modalities on datasets of noisy vs. ideal output distributions.
Train models to take noisy measured distributions as input and predict mitigated (closer-to-ideal) output distributions.
Identify sequence-to-sequence attention-based models as consistently superior on the tested datasets.
impact: Offers a practical classical post-processing method for near-term quantum devices, enabling AI/ML practitioners to obtain higher-fidelity outputs for quantum experiments and downstream quantum-enhanced workflows.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing error metrics (e.g., KL divergence, total variation distance) across model families (FCNN → Transformer).
Before/after probability distribution plots showing noisy vs. mitigated vs. ideal outputs for representative circuits.
Schematic diagram of a sequence-to-sequence attention model mapping noisy measurement sequences to mitigated distributions.
Pipeline/workflow icon: quantum circuit → measurement (noisy) → trained DL model → mitigated output → downstream task.
paper_title: Deep Learning Approaches to Quantum Error Mitigation
paper_authors: Leonardo Placidi, Ifan Williams, Enrico Rinaldi, Daniel Mills, Cristina Cîrstoiu
